messages:
Chris (CEO): thanks for the great questions earlier, leaving the thread open for follow-ups on GPUs/regions/autoscale. i'll try to answer the high-level asks first, then we can hand off to infra.
Maya (Infra PM): TL;DR: apac prewarm will start phased next quarter, t4 burst is still our primary short-term strategy, dedicated contracts unaffected. more below. :point_down:
Devon (Eng-SRE): quick ask — when we say 'phased', does that mean per-region toggles or org-by-org enabling?
Maya (Infra PM): per-region toggles. we'll enable apac -> then monitor queue depth, latency, and cost metrics for 2 weeks before widening scope.
Priya (Capacity): procurement update: t4 supply forecast improved by ~12% for Q2 thanks to a new vendor slot, ETA mid-May. still cautious on tpu-like capacity for larger sequences.
Jamal (SRE Lead): question: what are the autoscaler fallback priorities? e.g. if apac pool empty -> try eu -> try hosted cheap? need explicit order.
Maya (Infra PM): current policy is: region-local spare -> regional buffer pool -> cross-region fallthrough (with locality tag) -> hosted on-demand (last resort). order can be overridden per-customer via routing policy.
Devon (Eng-SRE): can we get that as a stub config so teams can test? something like:
```
routing.fallback_order: ["local_buffer", "region_buffer", "cross_region", "hosted_on_demand"]
``` 
Maya (Infra PM): yes, we'll publish the runbook + sample config in the console next week. CC @Priya for cost estimates per step.
Priya (Capacity): noted — expect a 30–60% cost uplift when crossing into hosted_on_demand depending on model and batch size. we'll attach per-model multipliers.
Linh (Support): heads-up from support: two customers asked about SLA impact during cross-region failover. they want clear messaging and an escalation path.
Chris (CEO): messaging is key. Maya — please draft a short FAQ and escalation matrix. include expected latency delta and a sample incident playbook.
Maya (Infra PM): will do. draft ETA: Friday EOD. will include a simple table: expected latency % increase, cost delta, and recommended canary settings.
Devon (Eng-SRE): tiny nit — canary settings should mention KV-cache warmup window and safe rollout % for large-context models.
Maya (Infra PM): agreed. adding rollout examples: 5% canary -> 25% after 24h -> 100% after 72h, with auto-rollback on error spikes.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: zone-fallback-policy v1.3 -> canary 5% -> start 1754340000. (automated message)
Jamal (SRE Lead): ops-bot — please include a link to the canary dashboard in the deploy note. also, include the synthetic prompt set we use for quality regression checks.
ops-bot: updated deploy note: dashboard -> https://console.internal/jobs/1754340000, synthetic set: infra_canary_v2
Devon (Eng-SRE): last question: prewarm sizing — are we prewarming per-customer or shared warm pools? which isolation level?
Priya (Capacity): hybrid approach: shared warm pools for base-load; optional customer-reserved prewarm for enterprise customers (extra charge, reservation API). we'll document limits and reservation flow.
Linh (Support): i'll update the support playbook once the FAQ lands. can someone flag me when the runbook is published? @Maya
Maya (Infra PM): tagging Linh on the PR. thanks everyone — i'll post the FAQ + runbook link here when live. :thumbsup:
Chris (CEO): appreciated. if leadership needs to follow up with specific customers, ping me and i'll join. good thread.
